code_snippet: export function isLocalVoice(provider: string, modelId: string, trusted: TrustedConfig): boolean { ... return decl.modelGroups[modelId] === "local"; ... }
finding: Under hounfour.locality: local_voices, Bridgebuilder's isLocalVoice/applyLocality decide locality from dispatch_group alone and never inspect the model entry's fallback_chain; cheval (chain_resolver.py:92) walks that chain inside one call, so a local voice whose chain names a hosted hop sends the PR content to a hosted provider when the local server fails.
reasoning_trace: Read config.ts:722-751; compared with hop-locality.py:16-17,123-133 (fallback_chain_reaches_hosted) and bats LOC-7; confirmed Bridgebuilder voices dispatch via cheval-delegate.ts --model provider:model and that chain_resolver.py appends the primary's fallback_chain. Cross-model DISS-C-003 raised the same chain walk.
critique: Three of four local_voices consumers honour the fallback-chain rule; Bridgebuilder does not.
remediation: Parse models.<id>.fallback_chain into ProviderDecl and recurse in isLocalVoice (unresolved or non-local hop => hosted, depth-bounded), or shell out to hop-locality.py; add a trusted-config.test.ts case mirroring LOC-7.

code_snippet: def _transport_policy(self, model_config): if getattr(self.config, "allow_insecure_endpoint", None) or getattr(model_config, "dispatch_group", None) == "local": return TransportPolicy(...)
finding: The D-7.2 request-time rules (no proxy env, no redirects, declared path prefix) are constructed only by OpenAIAdapter, while endpoint_policy.validate_providers admits allow_insecure_endpoint and dispatch_group: local for any non-CLI provider type; anthropic/google adapters call http_post/http_post_stream/http_get without policy.
reasoning_trace: base.py:270,378,468 policy param optional; grep of anthropic_adapter.py/google_adapter.py shows no policy argument; endpoint_policy.py:153-156 checks type only via _is_cli_provider.
critique: Documented guarantee (endpoint_policy.py:26-28) holds for one adapter family.
remediation: Refuse the opt-in / dispatch_group local at load for provider types whose adapter lacks the policy, or build the policy in ProviderAdapter so every adapter gets it; add a load test for the refused shape.

code_snippet: // Head-only refusal: on a PR the head checkout is attacker-controlled. ... keylessOnlyInHead || insecureOnlyInHead
finding: The trusted-configuration layer (D-7.5) refuses head-only keyless/insecure declarations but never compares endpoint or auth; every voice dispatches through cheval, which loads the checkout's .loa.config.yaml and (endpoint-validator.py:1291) admits any declared https host, so a PR head can repoint a credentialed built-in provider at a host it controls and the key plus the diff are sent there. Pre-existing exposure; the new mitigation leaves it open while README/SKILL.md describe providers as read from trusted config only.
reasoning_trace: config.ts:605-712 (trusted view = keyless, insecure, authEnv, dispatch groups only); cheval-delegate.ts:146 passes --model to cheval; loader.py:704 validate_providers -> validate_declared_endpoint skips step 8 allowlist; SKILL.md:116-118 notes the shipped model has no PR-head checkout. Cross-model DISS-C-005 raised the allowlist omission.
critique: Mitigation is incomplete for the threat model it states.
remediation: Have Bridgebuilder pass the trusted provider block to cheval (e.g. a config override path) or refuse a voice whose head endpoint/auth differ from the trusted declaration; on the cheval side WARN or refuse when a credentialed ({env:}) provider's https host is outside the canonical allowlist unless declared in a user/system layer.

finding: Three definitions of local: the planners (hop-locality.py:116, config.ts:730-732) accept a provider-level dispatch_group or all-models-local, cheval's loader requires the model-level key (loader.py _validate_model_auth_metadata) and ModelConfig/MODELINV read only the model entry (cheval.py:541, modelinv.py:473-475).
reasoning_trace: Read all three readers; the review reproduced CONFIG-INVALID for a provider-level-only key. Cross-model DISS-C-004.
critique: A hop can be planned local, refused by cheval at load, and recorded hosted in MODELINV.
remediation: Drop the provider-block rule from both planners (model-level only) or make cheval honour it everywhere.

finding: allow_insecure_endpoint is independent of keyless: a provider with an http RFC1918 endpoint and auth: {env:VAR} loads and the adapter sends the Bearer credential in cleartext (openai_adapter.py:172-173); no WARN at load.
reasoning_trace: validate_providers couples nothing; the example config (.loa.config.yaml.example:1235-1237) explicitly invites a keyed local server. Cross-model DISS-C-001.
remediation: WARN (or refuse) at load when an opted-in http provider is not keyless, and name the env var.

code_snippet: return "response_format" in text or "json_schema" in text
finding: The schema-rejection heuristic is a substring scan of the whole HTTP 400 body; any 400 whose text mentions response_format/json_schema (including an echoed prompt) triggers one retry without the schema, so the server can downgrade enforcement and double the request; recorded in telemetry only.
remediation: Match the structured error (error.param == response_format / error.code unsupported_parameter) and surface schema_rejected_by_server to the caller.

code_snippet: if _optin_raw is not None: _optin = _check_endpoint(...) if prov.get("endpoint") else None
finding: The defence-in-depth re-check in _build_provider_config runs only when an opt-in is present; a hand-built config with an http/loopback endpoint and no opt-in reaches ProviderConfig unchecked, and a lone opt-in with no endpoint is not validated.
reasoning_trace: cheval.py:546-557; load_config is the real gate (loader.py:704). Cross-model DISS-C-006.
critique: Gap only matters when load_config is bypassed.
remediation: Call check_endpoint unconditionally for non-CLI providers with an endpoint; validate a lone opt-in via canonical_optin_host.

finding: describe-provider prints the post-interpolation endpoint verbatim and _main prints str(exc) on load failure (line 224); the probe logs the URL (model-health-probe.sh:1505). interpolate_config is eager for every string except providers.*.auth, so an endpoint template embedding {env:TOKEN} leaks the value into probe logs/CI output.
critique: Docstring says never carries a secret.
remediation: Emit scheme/host/port via split_url as destination_for does; redact load errors.

finding: _probe_configured validates a configured provider's /models URL with the host allowlist, while cheval admits an operator-declared https host via validate_declared_endpoint; a hosted open-weight API that loads in cheval is answered UNKNOWN / endpoint_refused by the probe.
remediation: Pass a declared-endpoint mode to the validator CLI for configured providers, or document the allowlist requirement.
